title: What he looks for in a sideman
summary: He wants basics, time, respect for music and the right mental attitude, naming Hilton Jefferson, Ellis Larkin, Jimmy Jones, Billy Taylor Jr., Joe Wilder and Harold Mabern.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: One of the things I'm curious about in general is side men, people you've played with over the years. In general, what do you look for in a side man and who are some of the people who have responded best to you.

Well, I look for a side man to know all his basics and to have true respect for music in his heart. And I look for time and I look for the right mental attitude, that music is one of the true art forms of all civilization. You know there are certain people that have that. Now Hilton Jefferson had it, you know, I had the pleasure of playing with him. We did some record dates together. He had that all his life; he was totally dedicated. And, of course, Ellis Larkin. He is so impeccable. And Jimmy Jones. Billy Taylor, Jr., the bass player who died. He knew all of Duke Ellington's music; his father played with Duke. But

he knew all of Duke Ellington's music when he was a young man; he knew Ellington's music from 1922. And he impressed me very much. And then there was of course Cozy Cole, very dedicated. Oh, let's see. Joe Wilder, very dedicated. Of course Dizzy, very dedicated. In my life, I look at people like that and they are on their own case at all times. Oh, let's see if I can think of some other people.
I'm thinking of musically as well as...

Harold Mabern. He's dedicated. It's a pleasure playing with him. These are people I had the pleasure of playing with, because of their sincerity and dedication to music, you know. You can tell. There's no falseness there and they want to make sure they do everything right at all times, you know. And let's see. J.J. Johnson, Max Roach. Miles Davis. He's dedicated.
